answer: Sybil resistance works when identity carries a cost that cannot be recycled. An agent joins by posting a small slashable bond plus one-time proof of work, then starts dim: a lantern with no oil, earning nothing until independent peers countersign its output. Reputation flows only through attested tasks, so clones share one score instead of multiplying it. A comet of fresh accounts arriving together stands out, since their capital locks up and uncountersigned work stays worthless. Operators treat the network as a garden they prune, slashing any identity that vouches for its own duplicates.
